egress: NONE beyond Opal AWS. No call to Black Diamond by any route.
bounds_note: The repo copy of the shared ingest script lives under data/cot/, which BOUNDS clause 2 excludes. The DEPLOYED copy at s3://opal-data-bd/code/bronze/cot_bronze_ingest.py was read instead, which is also the authoritative instrument: the runner downloads it at runtime, so the repo copy is not what executes.

morning.transport: REST over HTTPS. Black Diamond DataMining REST API at https://bd3.bdreporting.com. No browser, no Playwright, no portal login. Four endpoints in order: GET /datamining/auth/token (Cookie-authorized) -> {access_token}; POST /datamining/request/v1/run {template, asOfDate} (Bearer) -> {templateId, resultGuid}; GET /datamining/request/v1/run/{runId}/status (Bearer) -> {statusMessage, isComplete}; GET /Api/DataMining/ExportResults/{resultGuid} (Cookie) -> xlsx bytes. Client is urllib.request in cot_bronze_ingest.py _request, HTTP_TIMEOUT_S=120, status poll every 5s to a 900s timeout.
morning.auth: A .bd.identity session cookie jar in Secrets Manager secret blackdiamond/49f/session, written by the session-fetch leg and extended by bd-49f-keepalive. The full 7-cookie jar is sent because POST v1/run needs .AspNetCore.Antiforgery and idsrv, not .bd.identity alone. A DataMining bearer is minted per run from that cookie; a 401 mid-sweep re-mints once before cookie-death is concluded, bounded by MAX_RETRIES=3.
morning.entry_point: Lambda bd-49f-runner (infra/aws/lambda/bd-pipeline/bd-49f-runner/lambda_function.py). It downloads the shared engine s3://opal-data-bd/code/bronze/cot_bronze_ingest.py at runtime and orchestrates per table. Terraform infra/aws/terraform/bd-pipeline/bd-49f-interim.tf.
morning.schedule: EventBridge rule bd-49f-session-daily cron(0 0 * * ? *) ENABLED, via bd-49f-session-trigger; the belt rule bd-49f-runner-daily cron(0 2 * * ? *) is DISABLED. Session plumbing bd-49f-keepalive on rule bd-49f-keepalive-sched rate(15 minutes) ENABLED. Measured runner start times 00:01-00:03Z.
morning.firm_separation: All four env vars set explicitly in the runner before the shared module imports (BD_S3_BUCKET=opal-data-bd, BD_FIRM_ID=49f, BD_SESSION_SECRET_ID=blackdiamond/49f/session, BD_BASE=https://bd3.bdreporting.com); the engine re-asserts fail-closed via _assert_firm_separation().

completeness_chain.per_table_sidecar: forwardfill_v2/<table>/_complete/<as_of>.json carrying has_data_rows, landed_at, bytes, basis (land_time_measured or content_probe_backfill) and inferred. Read verbatim: {"date": "2026-10-06", "table": "transactions", "has_data_rows": 0, "landed_at": "2026-10-06T00:01:37Z", "bytes": 4357, "basis": "land_time_measured", "inferred": false}.
completeness_chain.sentinel: bronze/<run_date>/_BRONZE_COMPLETE.json, emitted by emit_bronze_sentinel only when every table in the run landed AND each sidecar attests >=1 data row. The S3 notification BronzeCompleteSilverMerge then fires Lambda bd-silver-merge, which runs s3://opal-data-bd/code/silver/merge-daily-incremental.py over all four tables.
completeness_chain.measured_gap: bronze/ census 2026-09-03..2026-10-06 = 34 dates; _BRONZE_COMPLETE present 23, ABSENT 11. The absent dates: 09-07 Mon, 09-08 Tue, 09-09 Wed, 09-14 Mon, 09-15 Tue, 09-21 Mon, 09-22 Tue, 09-28 Mon, 09-29 Tue, 10-05 Mon, 10-06 Tue. Cause on those dates: the newest transactions tile is a 4,357-byte header-only export with has_data_rows 0, so the sentinel is withheld and bd-silver-merge never fires. 10-06 is the day of measurement and its evening run (21:45Z/21:53Z) was not yet due when this was read.
completeness_chain.partial_sentinel: On a day where the two snapshot tables are rejected but transactions has rows, the sentinel still fires naming only the tables that landed: bronze/2026-10-03/_BRONZE_COMPLETE.json reads artifacts.count 2, tables [transactions, realized], so silver advances with allocations and unrealized unrefreshed.

measured_cadence.transactions: DAILY. 105 TRANSACTIONS_DAILY_* objects; 36 as-of dates across 2026-09-01..10-06, one per calendar day. Each 00:0xZ run writes 5 tiles, so one as-of date is re-landed on several days.

measured_cadence.why_weekly: MEASURED, not inferred. CloudWatch /aws/lambda/bd-49f-runner carries one 'REJECTED <table> @as_of=<date> -- empty snapshot export, nothing landed' line per weekday run for BOTH tables (read 2026-10-06 for as_of 09-22, 09-23, 09-24, 09-25 and 09-28). Mechanism: the run fires 00:00Z = the prior 20:00 US Eastern, and the as-of lag of 1 business day asks BD for a snapshot only about 4 hours old in BD's business timezone; BD returns a 0-data-row export, which SNAPSHOT_TABLES reject pre-write. Only the Sunday run, which also resolves to Friday, asks for an as-of about 28 hours old and gets rows. The runner's own RESULT lines agree: run_date 10-01, 10-02, 10-03 and 10-06 each rejected [allocations, unrealized]; 10-04 landed all four with allocations and unrealized at as_of 2026-10-02; 10-05 skipped both as already-landed.
measured_cadence.already_recorded: The weekly cadence itself is already on the channel as NFRA_MCPINDEX-Z-W25-S2, which also records that silver/allocations is documented FROZEN at 2026-07-10 with the feed DEPRECATED. What is new here is the measured CAUSE and the per-run reject evidence; filed as NFRA_MCPINDEX-Z-S78 citing that row rather than as a fresh observation.

verdict.statement: EXTRANEOUS AS A SOURCE AND AS A SCHEMA; NOT YET REDUNDANT AS A SCHEDULER. The evening run fetches nothing from Black Diamond, reads the morning run's own bronze, and emits no field the morning path does not already emit. Its only non-redundant function today is to merge same-day on the dates the morning sentinel is withheld -- 11 of 34 dates in 2026-09-03..2026-10-06, chiefly Mondays and Tuesdays when BD posts transactions late. Close that gap and the run has no remaining function.

surprise_row_id_form_departure: The order's prescribed surprise-row id form, `NFRA_MCPINDEX-Z-AEMI-S<k>`, is REFUSED BY BOTH GATES and was not used; the rows carry NFRA_MCPINDEX-Z-S77..Z-S81 instead. Measured: surprise-row-gate.py:105 ID_RE = ^(?P<project>[A-Z0-9_]+)-(?P<z>Z-)?(?:W(?P<w>[0-9]+)-|(?P<c>C-))?S(?P<k>[0-9]+)$ and proof-of-spec-check.py:1198 SURPRISE_ID_RE = ^\s*([A-Z0-9_]+-(?:Z-)?(?:W[0-9]+-|C-)?S[0-9]+)\b both admit only an optional W<n>- or C- segment, so an `AEMI-` lane segment matches neither. Denominator: of the 243 rows in the channel, the 5 AEMI-form ids were the ONLY 5 the gate's ID_RE refused; 238 use an accepted form. Consequence had they stood: 5 ENFORCE violations on the SURPRISES limb, which per CLAUDE.md section 2 blocks this tree TO's `complete` flip -- verified by running the checker, which read exactly those 5 and nothing else. The lane identity the AEMI segment was carrying is not lost: it is in each row's `surfaced_by` (0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~MI), which is where it belongs. Reported to the issuer under BOUNDS clause 3 (refuse a criterion you cannot meet as written and report it with its measurement); the id-form prescription is the issuer's to correct in the order template.
